;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Noblesville West Middle School shooting]]
**A shooting at the Noblesville West Middle School in [[Noblesville, Indiana|Noblesville]], [[Indiana]], [[United States]], leaves two people injured. One suspect is in custody. [http://www.businessinsider.com/noblesville-school-shooting-indiana-2018-5 (''Business Insider'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the European Union]]
**[[European Union|EU]] [[finance minister]]s reach an agreement on reforming bank capital rules. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-eu-banks-regulation/eu-states-reach-deal-on-reform-of-banking-capital-rules-idUSKCN1IQ14X (Reuters)]
*[[Economy of Colombia]]
**The [[OECD]] member countries admit [[Colombia]] as its 37th member. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-05/26/c_137207054.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[Economy of Italy]]
**The [[yield spread]] between the [[Italia]]n and [[Germany|German]] 10-year [[List of government bonds|government bonds]] rises to over 2% for the first time in a year, due to the political uncertainty. [https://elpais.com/economia/2018/05/25/actualidad/1527233731_822514.html (''El País'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Transport in Uganda]]
**48 people die in an accident involving a tractor, a bus and a truck in [[Kiryandongo]], [[Western Region, Uganda|Western Region]]. [http://www.africanews.com/2018/05/26/uganda-48-people-killed-in-a-road-accident-red-cross/ (Africa News)]
*[[2018 lower Puna eruption]]
**A magnitude 4.4 earthquake occurs at [[Kīlauea]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/hawaii-kilauea-volcano-earthquake-today-2018-05-25/ (CBS News)]

;International relations
*[[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]]
**A senior [[Iran]]ian official asks European powers to come up with a "Plan B" before the end of May, so that Iran may decide 'within weeks' whether to stay in the agreement. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-talks/iran-sets-end-of-may-deadline-to-see-eu-measures-to-save-nuclear-deal-idUSKCN1IQ004 (Reuters)]
*[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] tweets that "very productive talks" are being held with [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong-un]] on reinstating the June 12  [[Singapore]] summit, which he had cancelled Thursday.  [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-44263045 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[General Data Protection Regulation]]
**GDPR rules come into effect in the European Union. Several U.S. news sites are subsequently taken offline in the [[United Kingdom]] and Europe, including the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' and [[Lee Enterprises]] newspapers. [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/gdpr-us-news-websites-la-times-offline-chicago-tribune-new-york-daily-a8368556.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Austria]]n privacy organization [[NOYB – European Center for Digital Rights|NOYB]] files complaints to regulators in four EU countries alleging that [[Facebook]], [[Google]], [[Instagram]], and [[WhatsApp]] are violating the GDPR. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-europe-privacy-lawyer/austrian-data-privacy-activist-takes-aim-at-forced-consent-idUSKCN1IQ0ZI (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-44252327 (BBC News)]
*[[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse allegations]]
**After surrendering to the [[New York City Police Department|NYPD]], film producer [[Harvey Weinstein]] is formally charged with [[rape]] and other sexual abuse offences involving two women. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-44257202 (BBC News)]
*Police in [[India]] state that mobs have killed three people after social media warned of roaming gangs of child kidnappers. They say that there is no evidence of such gangs. [http://www.tampabay.com/inflamed-by-social-media-mobs-kill-at-least--in-india-ap_world2af01417d5814f91a372bd7e3bc701c2 (''Tampa Bay Times'')]
*[[Bulgaria]]n customs agents seize {{convert|191|kg}} of [[heroin]] in transit for [[Belgium]] and the [[Netherlands]] at the border with [[Turkey]]. The drugs, with a street value of [[Euro|€]]6 million, were hidden under tile glue and detected by a [[detection dog|sniffer dog]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/bulgarian-customs-seize-191kg-of-heroin-bound-for-belgium/2018/05/25/5b30ab06-6037-11e8-b656-236c6214ef01_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Spain]], [[Gürtel case]]
**The opposition [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party|Socialist Workers' Party]] presents a [[motion of no confidence]] against [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Mariano Rajoy]] following the publication of the sentence in the [[Gürtel case|Gürtel corruption scandal]], which involved the ruling [[People's Party (Spain)|PP]]. [http://www.elmundo.es/espana/2018/05/25/5b07ce56468aeb4a7d8b46b2.html (''El Mundo'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/may/25/spanish-socialists-file-no-confidence-motion-against-mariano-rajoy-gurtel (''The Guardian'')]
**The [[Citizens (Spanish political party)|Citizens]] party gives an ultimatum to Rajoy to call snap elections or otherwise they'll support the motion of no confidence. [http://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20180525/443816310040/ciudadanos-ultimatum-rajoy-elecciones-mocion-de-censura.html (''La Vanguardia'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/25/world/europe/spain-rajoy-corruption.html (''The New York Times'')]
**Rajoy reaffirms that he will not resign, nor call elections and that the motion of no confidence is bad for the stability of the country. [https://politica.elpais.com/politica/2018/05/25/actualidad/1527233590_838146.html (''El País'')]
*[[Barbadian general election, 2018]]
**The [[Barbados Labour Party]], entering the election as the opposition party, wins all 30 seats in the [[House of Assembly of Barbados|House of Assembly]]. [[Mia Mottley]] becomes the first female [[Prime Minister of Barbados]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-barbados-election/barbados-opposition-wins-every-seat-in-landslide-election-victory-idUSKCN1IQ1N3 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of the Democratic Republic of the Congo]]
**[[Moïse Katumbi]] and [[Félix Tshisekedi]], two major opposition figures in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], issue a joint statement; they discuss choosing a single candidate to run in the [[President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|presidential]] [[Democratic Republic of the Congo general election, 2018|election]] now scheduled for December 23. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-25/congo-opposition-leaders-mull-unity-candidate-for-delayed-vote (Bloomberg)]
*[[Russian presidential election, 2024]]
**[[Russia]]n [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] says that he will respect the [[Constitution of Russia|Russian constitution]] and step down when his term expires in 2024. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-putin-rule-constitution/putin-says-will-step-down-as-president-after-term-expires-in-2024-idUSKCN1IQ2H9 (Reuters)]
*[[Thirty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution Bill 2018]]
**[[Ireland]] holds a referendum which will decide whether to repeal the [[Constitution of Ireland|constitution]]al prohibition of [[abortion]]. Exit polls suggest the results shall be 68% "yes" and 32% "no". The results will be released at 09:00 UTC tomorrow. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/irish-times-exit-poll-projects-ireland-has-voted-by-landslide-to-repeal-eighth-amendment-1.3508861 (''The Irish Times'')], [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-44241521 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[2018 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Subtropical Storm Alberto]] becomes the first named storm of the [[2018 Atlantic hurricane season]]. It formed at the western [[Caribbean Sea]] and is expected to move north of the [[Gulf of Mexico]] later in the weekend. [https://weather.com/storms/hurricane/news/2018-05-25-subtropical-tropical-storm-alberto-forecast-gulf-of-mexico-memorial (The Weather Channel)]
